explore.title: Run exploration cycles until the human converges or shelves
explore.imperative: Run repeatable exploration cycles; this step stays in-progress across cycles. Each cycle is its own survey (cycle-<N>.json in the work-area root, from templates/CYCLE.template.json), driven with constellation-interrogator doctrine loaded (one question at a time, recommended answers, code-answers-over-questions). At cycle start the human picks a flavor (shotgun | compare | refine; the agent may recommend). Run point-questions, then dispatch excursions as BACKGROUND subagents via py C:/Users/fredc/.claude/skills/constellation-explorer/scripts/run_crew.py (durable registry); run py C:/Users/fredc/.claude/skills/constellation-explorer/scripts/recover_crews.py explore-design-thrust before EACH dispatch and before consolidation so an in-flight excursion is never lost to a crash. Every excursion answers one named question and obeys scoped-nulls doctrine (a failed excursion kills THAT test under those conditions, never the idea class). Consolidate: cluster and cull ideas (culls stay on the board with reasons), fold in excursion findings, update IDEAS_BOARD.md. PREMATURE CONVERGENCE IS THE FAILURE MODE THIS STEP EXISTS TO PREVENT: never initiate convergence. Present each cycle's consolidated ideas and open threads; only the human says 'converge to spec' or 'shelve'. You may flag ripeness only as a standalone message containing nothing else. Record the human's converge/shelve decision as a user-decision evidence artifact (attach explore --type user-decision --field decision=...). This step closes ONLY on that decision AND the verify_cycles.py check: at least one cycle-*.json exists and every one carries a non-null consolidation — explore cannot close having run zero cycles or with an unconsolidated cycle.

review.title: Cold adversarial critical review
review.imperative: Dispatch a cold, full-adversary critic via templates/CRITIC_HANDOFF.template.md: the critic reads the spec with NO exploration record, nothing sacred, and may attack deliberate decisions; the human filters relitigation noise. Panel scaled by weight — default one critic; a spec that would spawn epics or touch architecture gets a 3-lens panel (intent-fit / testability / simplicity-YAGNI). When in doubt, panel. Every finding lands in the spec's structured findings table (fixed columns 'ID | Lens | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Reason'; Disposition in EDIT / RE-EXPLORE / REJECT) and the human triages each one. A RE-EXPLORE disposition is an engine reopen of the explore step: the inline rework cap is 99 so the critic->re-explore loop never hard-blocks, and the reopen cascade resets spec/review/confirm and supersedes their evidence — survivable because the ideas board is the source of truth and the spec re-crystallizes from it. This step closes only when every Disposition cell is filled, checked mechanically by verify_spec_confirmed.py --phase review.

confirm.title: Hard confirmation gate
confirm.imperative: The hard gate: no work is cut from an unconfirmed design. Fill the spec's Confirmation block — Status CONFIRMED, Confirmed by, Date — and record assumptions exercised vs accepted untested (accepting an untested load-bearing assumption is a visible, human-signed choice, never a silent skip). Get the human's explicit confirmation and record it as a user-decision evidence artifact (attach confirm --type user-decision --field decision=confirmed). Trust model, stated honestly: the engine records a user-decision rather than cryptographically proving a human made it; explorer has no delegated mode, so fabricating one violates doctrine an agent has no sanctioned path around — verify_spec_confirmed.py and the downstream UNCONFIRMED refusal are the mechanical backstops. This step closes on the user-decision artifact AND verify_spec_confirmed.py (Confirmation block filled: Status CONFIRMED with confirmer and date, and no empty Disposition cell).
